title: Prove the extraction changed nothing
description:
Re-derive and re-score against the frozen baseline. Identical output, or the extraction is wrong and gets reverted rather than patched.

This is the gate the whole project's evidence depends on: every number in FINDINGS was produced by the pre-move code.
acceptance_criteria: Re-scored dev and held-out match the baseline exactly; dev is 3.76s/0.51s for t3 as it is today; any difference blocks the merge.
notes:
INPUT FROM sp-79y.2's REVIEW (2026-09-19) — this is the central task of this bead, already scoped by execution.

The behavioural pin built during the move covers ONLY segments.derive/choose. A reviewer mutated the other moved modules and every mutation left the suite 86/86 GREEN: gutting blocks.speech_runs, features.describe and audio.envelope to raise, and shifting rules.TEACH_MIN_S, acoustic.MIN_DIP_DB, render.TARGET_I, classify.MAX_REPAIRS and segments.SPEAKER_SNAP_S. Seven of the nine moved modules have no behavioural net.

sp-79y.2 is nonetheless sound: its proof is byte-identity, independently verified by AST comparison of every function body plus a re-derivation of all 181 block files through the pre-move code rebuilt in /tmp (0 differences). But 'provably behaviour-preserving' currently rests on the git rename, not on a test — so any LATER refactor of this code is unguarded, and that is what this bead must fix.

Two things to know when building it. experiments/baseline.py is NOT sufficient alone: it fingerprints artefacts on disk and never imports or executes the pipeline, so it is blind to a changed boundary rule. And speaker_edges is measured dead on the current corpus (0/181 fingerprint differences with vs without diarization, because every value handed to snap() is already a transcript edge and the strict < locks speaker edges out) — so an end-to-end fingerprint cannot catch a DATA_ROOT regression, and that blind spot needs covering directly. The deadness is data-dependent, not structural: 15,013 speaker edges are genuinely not transcript edges and the nearest comes within 0.029 s, so any change to what snap() receives makes diarization live again.
close_reason: Verdict: nothing drifted. Data instrument exit 0, the boundary fingerprint reproduces all 181 stored block files, and a new behavioural net closes the gap the move's review found — seven of nine moved modules had no guard at all. Sixteen mutations are caught, fifteen behaviourally rather than by a value pin; verified independently by mutating blocks.GAP_S, rules.TEACH_MIN_S and render.LAME_Q together. Done as pure recomputation from stored artefacts: the bead's literal 're-derive and re-score' would have rewritten the 181 files that ARE the baseline and spent a held-out shot already spent. What cannot be pinned without ffmpeg or a model host is named rather than faked.

title: Freeze the current results as the extraction baseline
description: Before moving any code: capture the scored output of every stored config so the move can be proved identical. data/results.jsonl already holds it; snapshot the derived segments per config too, since rederive.py rewrites them in place.
acceptance_criteria: A committed baseline file covering all 181 stored results; a one-command comparison that reports any drift.
close_reason: experiments/baseline.py plus a committed 468 KB snapshot fingerprinting 34 MB of derived data: 232 scored rows whole, 181 block files as canonical digests plus the values rederive.py rewrites, transcripts and diarization as digests. One command reports drift; verified independently strict on value (1 ms change exits 1, naming file, field and digest) and quiet on representation (all 181 files reformatted, exits 0). Nothing re-derived, nothing scored, held-out budget untouched, no existing experiments file modified.

title: Move the library modules, no other change
description: audio, blocks, cues, segments, rules, features, acoustic, the render chain, the ollama client. Imports updated, nothing else touched — no renames, no comment cleanup, no refactoring. The argparse drivers stay in experiments/ and are left frozen.
acceptance_criteria: Every moved module imports from src/sermon/pipeline; experiments/ still runs; the diff contains only moves and import lines.
close_reason: The validated pipeline is extracted into src/sermon/pipeline: seven modules moved whole, the render chain and ollama client lifted out of their CLI drivers. Behaviour preservation verified independently two ways — AST comparison showing every moved function body byte-identical, and re-deriving all 181 stored block files through the pre-move code rebuilt in isolation for zero differences. Not a pure rename: three modules resolved data paths from __file__, so a verbatim move would have silently repointed them at a directory that does not exist; those roots are injected now, and fail loudly naming module and setting. Review also fixed a broken spike entry point, six frozen modules reaching undefended roots, and a static guard a comment could satisfy.

title: pytest-bdd harness over features/
description:
Point pytest-bdd at features/ so all 460 scenarios collect and fail as undefined rather than erroring. Register the spec tags as pytest marks (they warn otherwise). Wire features/validate_spec.py in as a test so the spec cannot silently stop parsing.

Verified already: the whole spec collects as 604 tests.
acceptance_criteria: `pytest --collect-only` reports 604 tests, 0 errors; validate_spec passes as a test; ADR-LS-001 Red phase is genuine (undefined, not error).
close_reason: pytest-bdd collects all 604 scenarios with no hand-maintained list; 17 spec tags registered as marks; validate_spec wired in as a test. Two review rounds closed nine execution-verified routes by which the suite could go green while the spec was silenced, hollowed or partly unread — spec size, step count (1898), executed-vs-skipped counts, deferral level, recursive step discovery, and hooks refused in step modules are each pinned by a guard test.

title: Extract the validated pipeline into the package
description:
experiments/src mixes library code with argparse CLI drivers. The product wants the library half.

Highest-risk task in the project: every number in FINDINGS rests on this code. The move must be provably behaviour-preserving and must NOT be combined with refactoring or comment cleanup.
notes:
Dependency corrected 2026-09-19: the edge on the Foundations EPIC was replaced with edges on the five Foundations children this work actually needs (sp-1vn.1 package skeleton, sp-1vn.2 the pytest-bdd harness, sp-1vn.3 the store, sp-1vn.5 config, sp-8z5 package-data), all closed. The epic itself stayed open only for the Dockerfile bead and two P3 nitpicks, none of which the extraction needs — and because the whole phase tree hangs off that epic, these P0 beads never appeared in bd ready for nine iterations while P2 and P3 work did. Depending on an epic makes a bead's readiness hostage to its least related sibling.
STATUS 2026-09-19: the extraction itself is complete and proven. sp-79y.1 (baseline), .2 (the move) and .3 (the proof) are closed. The epic stays open only for .4, the comment cleanup this epic deliberately forbade combining with the move.

.4 is now SAFE to do, and that is the point of the ordering: tests/test_pipeline_behaviour.py guards all nine moved modules (16 mutations caught, 15 behaviourally), so a cleanup pass can no longer change behaviour undetected. Before the net existed, seven of the nine modules had no guard and gutting three of them to raise left the suite green.

Scope for .4, measured on adoption: 239 comment lines at 6.3 percent density, 21 blocks over the three-line ceiling (worst 16 lines), 12 containing dates, 12 in 'Measured...' narrative voice, 5 using first person. Most duplicate FINDINGS.md, which is the diagnosis — the rationale already had a home and was written twice. Run the three instruments before and after: experiments/baseline.py, tests/test_pipeline_library.py (needs primary data) and tests/test_pipeline_behaviour.py.

description:

title: Three-click week: preview in, preview out, approve
description:
Governing file: features/interface/segment_review.feature
Rule: The ordinary week is three clicks
Scenario: Preview in, preview out, approve

Seed awaiting_review with the feature Background's two Segments. Given a sermon Segment whose cuts are both graded easy. Preview punch-in, preview punch-out, approve. Then a processing/render Job is queued and the waveform editor was not opened.

acceptance_criteria: Derived from segment_review.feature Rule 'The ordinary week is three clicks', scenario 'Preview in, preview out, approve'. Preview punch-in, preview punch-out, approve queues a render Job for that Segment and does not open the waveform editor.

title: Three-click week: analyze Job produces punch-in and punch-out
description:
Third scenario of the three-click week: the queued analyze Job runs far enough to produce punch-in and punch-out.

Governing file: features/analysis/analysis_orchestration.feature
Rule: The pipeline runs its stages in dependency order

The vertical slice named in CLAUDE.md continues here: a recording appears (sp-b41.2), the pipeline analyses it, a reviewer previews punch-in and punch-out, approves, an MP3 lands. This bead is only the analysis run that leaves a downloaded Recording with proposed Segments that have punch-in and punch-out. Do not decompose the rest of analysis. Do not implement per-Rule analysis beads.

Acceptance is the Gherkin, not an invented checklist. Out of scope: HTTP-only inference, speech-to-text hosting, model-host unreachability, stage-output retention for re-runs, skipped Segments remaining stored, re-running Analysis after human work, stage failures, time budget, FLAC immutability, review UI, render, ingestion decomposition.

Parent epic sp-3wf is the phase home. This task must not depend on that epic (or on extraction epic sp-79y). The store, package, webhook, and download work are already closed. Tests may seed a downloaded Recording and a queued analyze Job directly; they do not have to go through webhook or download.

The extracted pipeline in src/sermon/pipeline/ is not the work. Do not modify it. Inject stage implementations so tests do not call ollama, whisper, or real audio. The Background "it contains a 9:00 class and the 10:30 service" is a Given: the test tells analysis what is in the recording. Production later replaces the stubs; this bead only has to run the Job, record stage order, store Segments with punch-in/punch-out, and leave the Recording awaiting_review.
acceptance_criteria:
Derived from features/analysis/analysis_orchestration.feature, Rule "The pipeline runs its stages in dependency order", the two scenarios that produce punch-in and punch-out. Acceptance criteria derived from those Gherkin scenarios because this bead had none until filed.

1. Given a Recording in state downloaded that is 3:12:00 long and contains a 9:00 class and the 10:30 service, and a queued Job of kind analyze for that Recording, when Analysis starts (the analyze Job runs), the Recording enters "analyzing", then the stages run in this order: envelope, probe, waveform, preview, transcription, diarization, blocking, block_classification, summarization, segment_proposal, boundary_refinement, scoring. Blocking and block_classification iterate until stable. When scoring completes the Recording enters "awaiting_review". A notification is sent to the reviewers (publishable Segments were found).

2. When Analysis completes, 2 Segments exist. Each Segment has its own punch-in, punch-out, classification and confidence. Each Segment is independently dispositionable: approving one does not affect the other.

pytest-bdd step definitions for those two scenarios FAIL (not ERROR) in Red, then pass in Green. Other orchestration Rules stay unimplemented. The other two scenarios of this Rule (stage-output retention; skipped Segments remaining) stay unimplemented.

Restarted 2026-09-20: three overlapping implementers on this worktree were aborted; branch reset to 627e303 (v1-build). Next fire implements from Red.
Second triplicate abort 2026-09-20: orchestrator spawned 3 implementers because spawn_subagent is async. Branch reset to 627e303 again.

Other orchestration Rules stay red. Acceptance derived from analysis_orchestration.feature Rule 'The pipeline runs its stages in dependency order'.

title: Three-click week: download makes a Recording analysable
description:
Second scenario of the three-click week: the discovered Recording is downloaded so analysis can run.

Governing file: features/ingestion/recording_download.feature
Rule: A successful download makes the Recording analysable

The vertical slice named in CLAUDE.md continues here: a recording appears (sp-b41.2), the pipeline analyses it, a reviewer previews punch-in and punch-out, approves, an MP3 lands. This bead is only the download that makes a Recording analysable. Do not decompose the rest of ingestion.

Acceptance is the Gherkin, not an invented checklist. Out of scope: MD5 mismatch, undecodable audio, object-store retries, disk-full deadlock, byte-for-byte later-preservation, webhook idempotency, analysis execution, review, render.

Parent epic sp-b41 is the phase home. This task must not depend on that epic (or on extraction epic sp-79y). The store, package, and webhook create-Recording work are already closed. Tests may seed a discovered Recording directly; they do not have to go through the webhook.

Measured (feature preamble): there is no metadata sidecar in the bucket. The sidecar-present path is still in this Rule and must be implemented; the missing-sidecar path is the production one.
acceptance_criteria:
Derived from features/ingestion/recording_download.feature, Rule "A successful download makes the Recording analysable":

1. Given a discovered Recording whose object key parses as recording_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS, when the download job runs, the Recording records started_at from the object key with started_at_source=key. No sidecar is required for that.

2. When the download job runs and a sidecar is present, the Recording moves through "downloading" to "downloaded", the FLAC is stored in local working storage (local_path set), sidecar fields duration/sample_rate/channels are parsed onto the Recording, sidecar_present is true, and an analyze Job is queued automatically (kind=analyze, state=queued). The HTTP/webhook path is not involved. Download does not run analysis.

3. When the object store has no sidecar, the Recording still reaches "downloaded", the missing sidecar is noted (sidecar_present=false), and technical metadata (duration, sample_rate, channels) is derived from the audio file itself. Do not overwrite a parseable key's started_at with last-modified solely because the sidecar is missing — DOMAIN.md and Scenario 1 of this Rule make the key the source of truth; last_modified is only for keys that do not parse.

pytest-bdd step definitions for those three scenarios FAIL (not ERROR) in Red, then pass in Green. Other download Rules stay unimplemented.
close_reason: Second three-click-week Rule: DownloadsRecording fetches the FLAC, moves discovered through downloading to downloaded, notes sidecar_present, stores duration/sample_rate/channels from sidecar or probe, and queues an analyze Job (pinned on the missing-sidecar production path). started_at stays the parseable object key, not sidecar recorded_at or last-modified — Gherkin Scenario 3 last Then is inverted to match DOMAIN.md; do not treat last-modified as a sidecar-missing fallback. Merged to tpett/ai/v1-build.

title: Three-click week: webhook creates a discovered Recording and queues download
description:
First scenario of the three-click week: a recording appears.

Governing file: features/ingestion/webhook_notification.feature
Rule: A valid webhook creates exactly one Recording

The vertical slice named in CLAUDE.md starts here: a recording appears, the pipeline analyses it, a reviewer previews punch-in and punch-out, approves, an MP3 lands. Do not decompose the whole ingestion phase into one bead per Rule. Implement this Rule only.

Acceptance is the Gherkin, not an invented checklist. Out of scope: idempotency, concurrency, malformed payloads, ignored event types, delivery retries, S3 reconciliation, download execution, analysis, review, render.

Parent epic sp-b41 is the phase home. This task must not depend on that epic (or on extraction epic sp-79y): those edges hide ready work behind bookkeeping. The store and package are already closed.
acceptance_criteria:
Derived from features/ingestion/webhook_notification.feature, Rule "A valid webhook creates exactly one Recording":

1. POST /api/webhooks/recordings with payload event=recording.uploaded, bucket, object_key, metadata_key, size_bytes, md5, recorded_at, duration, sample_rate, channels responds 202 Accepted.
2. A Recording is created in state discovered. recording_id is derived from the object key (recording_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS). started_at is parsed from the key with started_at_source=key. size_bytes is stored. local_path is null (no audio downloaded yet).
3. A Job of kind download, state queued, is stored for that Recording. The HTTP response has already returned; download does not run inline.
4. A webhook that omits host identity still responds 202 Accepted and the Recording is created with capture_device null.

pytest-bdd step definitions for those two scenarios FAIL (not ERROR) in Red, then pass in Green. Other webhook Rules stay unimplemented.
close_reason: First three-click-week scenario: POST /api/webhooks/recordings returns 202, stores a discovered Recording (id and started_at from the object key), queues a download Job, and treats host identity as optional. Acceptance derived from webhook_notification.feature Rule 'A valid webhook creates exactly one Recording'. Merged to tpett/ai/v1-build.

title: Nothing records the human-confirmed or corrected speaker
description: interface/segment_review.feature:191 'When I confirm or correct who was preaching / Then that Segment strengthens or creates that speaker's profile'. Only machine similarity is stored, so a human correction is invisible and the next re-analysis silently reverts it -- the exact failure Block.retyped_by_human exists to prevent. SpeakerProfile.confirmed_by_human records that a profile was confirmed, not which Segment's voice it corrects. This is adjacent to the harm case the spec already names: publishing under the wrong preacher's name.
acceptance_criteria: A human's speaker confirmation or correction is stored per Segment and survives re-analysis.
close_reason: Segment.confirmed_speaker_profile_id with a foreign key, so a human's correction of who preached survives a re-analysis that re-ranks the machine's similarity scores. distribution_confirmed was the consent half; this is the identity half.

title: NEW ENTITY: skipped object keys that can never become a Recording
description: ingestion/s3_reconciliation.feature:69,:83 'Then the object key and the reason are recorded / And an operator can see every object the Processor has ever skipped', with examples 'recording_19700101_000000.flac | recorder clock not set' and 'sermon-2027-01-03.flac | key does not match the pattern'. Recording.skip_reason cannot hold three of the four listed reasons: recording_id is derived from the key (unparseable in these cases) and started_at is NOT NULL, so no Recording row can exist for them at all.
acceptance_criteria: Every skipped object key and its reason are stored and listable, including keys no Recording can represent.
close_reason: SkippedObject keyed on the object key, with a CHECK-closed reason taken verbatim from the spec's own Examples table. Keyed on the key rather than a generated id because three of the four reasons describe keys no Recording row can exist for, and because a scheduled re-scan should correct its row rather than append one per scan. Reviewer attacked and approved the design: the scenarios name a set of objects and record the reason singular, so a timestamp would be a field no scenario forces.

title: NEW ENTITY: events that belong to no Recording
description: Three scenarios require recording something with no Recording to hang it on. ingestion/s3_reconciliation.feature:59 'Then the scan fails without changing any Recording state / And the failure is surfaced on the system health view'; :96 'And it is surfaced on the system health view as a credential problem'; webhook_notification.feature:102 'And the ignored event type is logged'. operations/system_health.feature:23 needs 'when the last webhook was received', 'when the last reconciliation scan ran' and 'how many recordings each discovered'. storage_and_retention.feature:66,:75,:91 raise disk-space alerts whose subject is the system. Both LogEntry.recording_id and Notification.recording_id are required FK columns, so none of this has a row it can be written as.
acceptance_criteria: Scan runs, webhook receipts and system-scoped alerts are stored and surface on the system health view.
close_reason: Discovery: one entity for scans and webhook receipts, since the health view renders them as one thing with one shared attribute. No Alert entity — the scenarios give an alert no fields of its own, so Notification.recording_id became nullable instead. Review proved that relaxation had turned an enforced guarantee into caller discipline; a new Presence primitive restores it in the schema and also forbids a webhook carrying a scan-only failure or a failed scan reporting discoveries.

title: ARTIFACT_KINDS has no envelope, the one output every later stage reads
description: analysis/analysis_orchestration.feature:58 lists 'envelope | the amplitude envelope every later stage reads' as the first stage, and :52 requires 'the stages already cached are not recomputed'. audio_probe.feature:147 'It reads the envelope already computed for the waveform'. vocabularies.ARTIFACT_KINDS has no envelope entry, so the stage output that the emptiness gate and boundary snapping both re-read cannot be stored, and the caching promise cannot be kept.
acceptance_criteria: An envelope artifact kind exists and the stages that read it do not recompute it.
close_reason: ARTIFACT_KINDS gains envelope, the first stage's output that every later stage re-reads and that the do-not-recompute promise depends on.

title: Recording cannot hold its source loudness measurements
description: analysis/audio_probe.feature:51 'Then the Recording records an integrated loudness in LUFS / And a true peak in dBTP / And a loudness range in LU / And these values are used as inputs to the render stage'. dynamic_range_db is the emptiness metric on a different scale; Artifact.render_settings is the render's target, not the source measurement. The render stage consumes these, so they cannot be recomputed later without re-probing.
acceptance_criteria: Recording carries integrated loudness, true peak and loudness range, and the render reads them.
close_reason: Recording carries integrated loudness, true peak and loudness range with units in the field names, so the render's normalization inputs cannot be confused with dynamic_range_db or with the render's own target.

title: Recording cannot hold per-channel levels or the mono-source decision
description: analysis/audio_probe.feature:28,:39 'Then the Recording records a per-channel RMS level' and 'And the Recording records that the render should use channel 1 only'. processing/audio_rendering.feature:29 adds 'And the reviewer is asked to confirm how it should be mixed to mono / Then the render does not start automatically'. The render BLOCKS on a human answer, so the decision must be stored -- it cannot be recomputed at render time.
acceptance_criteria: Per-channel RMS, the channel-or-mix decision, and whether a human answered it are all stored.
close_reason: Recording carries ordered per-channel levels, the channel-or-mix decision, and whether a human answered it — the render blocks on that answer so it cannot be recomputed. mono_source is open text, since the scenarios name one value and declare no vocabulary; a closed set would have been invented spec.

title: Segment has no span distinct from its punch points
description: interface/punch_point_adjustment.feature:201 'When I extend the Segment's own start to 1:26:00 / Then the Segment's span grows / And the change is rejected if it would overlap the neighbouring Segment'. The Scenario Outline at :190-198 rejects a punch-in at 1:20:00 because 'the boundary must fall within the Segment', and recording_detail.feature:11-13's Background carries separate 'spans' and 'boundaries' columns per Segment (lesson span 0:00:00-1:05:20, boundaries 0:04:10-1:03:55). I verified this myself: the model holds seed_block_id and no span, so the validation rule three interface scenarios depend on is currently unimplementable. Not derivable from seed_block_id -- a human extension would have to rewrite a machine-produced Block, and a meeting or hand-drawn Segment has no seed Block. Note analysis/segment_proposal.feature:206 reads the span AS the punch points; the two must be reconciled.
acceptance_criteria: Segment carries an outer span, punch points are constrained to fall inside it, and extension is rejected on overlap.
close_reason: Segment carries span_start_seconds/span_end_seconds, required because every Segment the spec creates has both ends. Two invariants deliberately deferred rather than dropped: punch points inside the span (sp-6kh, amended to name it) and overlap rejection on extension, which compares two rows (sp-wpw). segment_proposal.feature:206 resolved as not a contradiction — a merge and a hand-drawn Segment start coincident; a proposed Segment's span is detected and normally wider.

title: Segment has no summary
description: analysis/summarization.feature:28 'Then each proposed Segment carries its own summary / And the summary is shown beside it in the review interface / And it is shown in the notification'. Notification.summary is composed delivery text (DOMAIN.md:188), not the Segment's own line, and Block summaries do not compose into one.
acceptance_criteria: Segment.summary exists, round-trips, and is what the review interface and the notification show.
close_reason: Segment.summary, distinct from Notification.summary which is composed delivery text.

title: Derive the full field inventory from all 460 scenarios in one pass
description:
Every batch that tries to persist something finds another thing the spec requires and DOMAIN.md cannot hold. Twelve so far across three batches: the Notification entity, Segment date and label, per-approval consent, speaker match confidence, proposal history, the processing log, the alternative punch-in candidate, boundary provenance, the capture device, the clipping flag, the failure reason, per-stage naming. Each was found only by attempting the store work, one batch at a time, at roughly a full review cycle each.

The cause is that DOMAIN.md was written as a summary of the entities rather than derived exhaustively from the scenarios, so the gaps are invisible until something tries to store them. The sp-dzc integrity bead samples IMPLEMENTED scenarios against their step definitions and would not catch these, because nothing is implemented yet.

Do the exhaustive pass once: walk every Rule in all 34 feature files, list every noun a scenario asserts is stored, shown, recorded, flagged or remembered, and diff that list against DOMAIN.md's seven-plus-two entities. Output is a gap list, not an implementation -- each real gap becomes its own bead. Cheaper than continuing to find them one batch at a time, and it also tells us when we are actually done.
acceptance_criteria: A gap list covering all 34 feature files exists, every entry either has a bead or a stated reason it needs none, and a re-run finds nothing new.
close_reason: Both halves of the spec audited exhaustively: 460 scenarios across all 34 feature files, 181 interface/operations/notifications and 279 ingestion/analysis/processing. Result: 21 certain gaps and 19 arguable, all filed. Five entities are unmodelled (skipped object keys, events belonging to no Recording, the reviewer, the accuracy corpus, retained suite results); Segment has no span distinct from its punch points, which makes a validation rule three interface scenarios depend on unimplementable; and five DOMAIN.md statements are stale or falsified by scenarios. Seven feature files were confirmed fully covered by the current model.

title: The processing log is required by the spec and modelled nowhere
description:
Four feature files require a per-attempt, per-transition record that no entity holds. interface/recording_detail.feature wants each state transition with its timestamp, each job attempt, and who performed each human action against which Segment. operations/system_health.feature wants per-attempt timestamp, duration and error. analysis_orchestration.feature promises 'the retry is visible in the Recording's processing log', and segment_proposal.feature refers to it too. Job holds only the current attempt count and last error -- never a per-attempt record -- and nothing holds state transitions or human actions at all.

Deliberately left out of the sp-9dl Proposal-history work rather than arriving as a logging subsystem side effect, and it also has to carry the boundary and adjustment history that reprocessing.feature wants (which needs an approver and a time nothing currently holds), so it wants designing once. It is listed in DOMAIN.md's 'What this model deliberately does not decide' -- which is precisely the mechanism by which the Notification entity went missing, so this should not sit there long.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md models the processing log with every field the four feature files require, and the store persists it.
close_reason: LogEntry models the processing log as one entity: state transitions, job attempts, human actions and boundary sets in one ordered table, with correlation_id NOT NULL so an entry can be tied to the application logs. One table rather than three because the spec expands one log and calls its unit an entry, and because one query then returns the whole log in time order.

title: Per-approval distribution consent is not recorded anywhere
description: interface/segment_review.feature, Rule 'I am told whose voice this is before I publish it': when a Segment's teaching voice matches no enrolled profile and its intent is publish, the reviewer is asked to confirm the recording may be distributed, and 'the confirmation is recorded with the approval'. No DOMAIN.md field records that per-Segment consent. SpeakerProfile.confirmed_by_human is about the profile, not about this approval. The scenario's own comment calls this 'the one place the system can cause real harm: a guest preacher who asked not to be distributed, approved ten days later by a reviewer who has forgotten' -- so the safeguard is exactly the thing the domain model does not store.
acceptance_criteria: The approval records the distribution confirmation, and the store persists it.
close_reason: Segment.distribution_confirmed records per-approval consent as a tri-state: null never asked, false declined, true confirmed. Verified unlosable — all three round-trip identity-preserved and a CHECK refuses anything else through raw SQL.

title: Segment has no Date or Label field, but the render filename needs both
description: interface/publication_details.feature requires a Date and a Label saved with the Segment -- the output MP3 filename is built from them, matching the corpus convention '2026-09-13 - Hebrews 12.25-29.mp3'. DOMAIN.md's Segment section has no field for either. This blocks the render naming rules in processing, and is the largest of the domain gaps found while building the store.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md's Segment carries the publication date and label, and the store persists them.
close_reason: Segment.publication_date and label, both nullable because required is a condition of publishing. The DDL generator gained a real date type rather than reusing datetime, since the filename convention is a calendar date.

title: Notification is fully specified but absent from DOMAIN.md
description: features/notifications/approval_notifications.feature specifies a Notification entity with an explicit field table (subject, kind, recipient, summary, created_at, state) and four states (pending, delivered, failed, suppressed), under the Rule 'A Notification is a record, not a message'. DOMAIN.md models seven entities and does not mention it, and its 'What this model deliberately does not decide' section does not list it either -- so this is an omission, not a decision. analysis_orchestration.feature also promises 'a notification is sent to the reviewers unless nothing publishable was found'. Consequence: the store built in sp-1vn.3 cannot persist a Notification, and the notifications feature file cannot be implemented until the entity exists. Verified: zero mentions of 'notification' in DOMAIN.md; state values 'suppressed' and 'failed' appear in features/ but in no DOMAIN.md or README table.
acceptance_criteria: DOMAIN.md models Notification with every field its feature file's table names, and the store persists it with its states closed.
close_reason: Notification modelled with every field its feature file's table names, state closed on the four verbatim values, subject as recording_id plus nullable segment_id following Artifact and Job. Delivery concerns disclosed in a Not stored note rather than silently omitted.

title: Integrity check: do step definitions assert what the Gherkin says?
description:
Recurring guard against the failure this whole arrangement exists to prevent: a suite that goes green while meaning nothing. Sample the scenarios implemented since the last integrity check, read each against its step definitions, and ask only whether the assertion is as strong as the Gherkin. A step that passes while testing something weaker is an IMPORTANT finding and becomes a bead.

Re-open and re-run this every ten bead closures. Do not close it permanently.
acceptance_criteria: A named sample of at least 8 implemented scenarios reviewed; for each, a verdict on whether its step definitions assert the full Gherkin; every weakening filed as a bead; the sample and verdicts recorded in the close reason.

Deferred so it is not picked up before there is anything to check. The loop re-opens it (bd update sp-dzc --defer=none) after every ten bead closures.
Re-opened at 19 closures per the loop rule and found nothing to sample: all 597 spec tests still fail as undefined, so zero scenarios are implemented. The only modules in tests/steps/ are the two discovery proofs from sp-1vn.2, which are harness self-tests rather than spec steps. Re-deferred rather than run.

  3. Two assertions were vacuous or tautological: one comparing unrelated literals, one restating a definition verbatim.
So this check should sample store tests as well as step definitions, and its method should include mutation -- break the thing the test claims to cover and confirm the test fails. Reading a test is not enough; all three of the above read fine.

title: Notification.kind being open is untested
description:
Integrity sample 9: DOMAIN.md Notification.kind is deliberately not a closed set because the scenarios raise notifications for many reasons and declare a vocabulary for none of them. LogEntry.kind is open for the same reason.

Weakening: nothing asserts openness. CLOSED_COLUMNS covers notification.state but not kind. Fixtures only use segment_proposed, nothing_publishable, scratch_exhausted, analysis_failed.

Mutation that stayed green: schema.TABLES[Notification].closed gained kind = those four values. 107 tests stayed green, including test_a_closed_column_refuses_a_value_the_spec_does_not_declare, test_a_closed_column_accepts_every_value_the_spec_declares, tests/test_store_vocabularies.py, tests/test_domain_md.py, and tests/test_sends_notification.py.

Same shape likely applies to LogEntry.kind (used values: approved, state_change, analyze_attempt, punch_in_adjusted, boundaries_proposed, boundaries_refined, adjustment_discarded, rendered) — not separately mutated.
acceptance_criteria: A test stores a Notification kind (and LogEntry kind) that is not among the currently used fixtures and fails if kind is added to schema.closed; or schema tests assert kind is absent from Table.closed.

title: ExtendsSegmentSpan success is not asserted as stored
description:
Integrity sample 1: Gherkin scenario Extending a Segment beyond its detected span (features/interface/punch_point_adjustment.feature) and the success-path tests in tests/test_extends_segment_span.py.

Weakening: the When claims the Segment's start is extended to 1:26:00, but nothing reloads the grown span from the store. Then "the Segment's span grows" only compares the return value to the original. Then "the punch-in may now be placed anywhere within the new span" calls PlacesPunchIn on the in-memory grown Segment, which saves the whole object, so a later store.loads of span_start_seconds == 1:26:00 still passes. Overlap tests only cover the refusal path.

Mutation that stayed green: ExtendsSegmentSpan.__call__ returns `proposed` without calling store.saves(). tests/test_spec.py::test_extending_a_segment_beyond_its_detected_span and all 10 tests in tests/test_extends_segment_span.py stayed green (11 passed).

Contrast: dropping the overlap check failed the Gherkin last Then and the refusal unit tests; saving then raising on overlap failed the Gherkin last Then and test_the_stored_span_is_unchanged_when_overlap_is_refused. Those claims HOLDS. The success-path persist does not.
acceptance_criteria: A successful extend is reloaded from the store, so skipping store.saves() fails the Gherkin scenario Extending a Segment beyond its detected span. Do not weaken the overlap Then.

title: SendsNotification tests never reload stored Notification state
description:
Samples:
- tests/test_sends_notification.py::test_sending_with_no_channel_configured_does_not_fail claims approval_notifications.feature 'No channel configured' (recorded, left undelivered, visible, nothing fails).
- tests/test_sends_notification.py::test_a_notification_already_pending_is_not_sent_after_opt_out asserts pending.state == 'pending' on the in-memory argument.

Mutation that stayed green: SendsNotification always stored state=delivered, including when the reviewer had opted out and when the default channel was a no-op. All five tests in the file passed. The no-channel test only asserts the return value; the pending test only asserts the object it passed in.

'No further notifications are sent' itself holds: always-calling sends() failed test_no_further_notifications_are_sent_after_opting_out and the pending test on the sent list.
acceptance_criteria: No-channel and opt-out send tests reload the stored Notification and assert it is not delivered when nothing was sent. A mutation that saves state=delivered without calling sends() must fail.

title: Cannot-be-aligned corpus test asserts the pair is listed, not excluded from ground truth
description:
Sample: tests/test_store.py::test_a_pair_that_cannot_be_aligned_is_excluded_from_the_corpus_and_the_exclusion_is_reported claims detection_accuracy.feature 'A pair that cannot be aligned' Then 'that pair is excluded from the corpus' And 'the exclusion is reported rather than silently dropped'.

The test stores alignment='cannot be aligned' with null punch points and asserts store.lists(CorpusPair) == [excluded]. That is the reported half. The excluded-from-the-corpus half is not independently asserted: the pair remains in the corpus table, and unlike test_a_published_output_that_covers_more_than_95_percent_of_its_source_is_flagged_rather_than_silently_accepted there is no labelled/ground-truth filter that would go red if scoring included it.

Mutation that stayed green relative to the exclusion claim: any ground-truth query that treats alignment='cannot be aligned' as a labelled example. The current assertions would still pass.
acceptance_criteria: The test has a ground-truth filter that omits alignment='cannot be aligned' pairs (as the 95-percent and machine-cut tests omit flagged/machine pairs). A scoring query that included cannot-be-aligned rows as labelled examples must fail.

comments.author: Travis Petticrew
comments.text: 2026-09-20: still true. The Gherkin Then “the pair is excluded from the corpus” still asserts the pair is stored with alignment="cannot be aligned". There is still no ground-truth query that would go red if scoring included it. Machine-cut provenance (excluded from ground truth for self-produced MP3s) is a different scenario and does not close this weakening.

title: Drift store test restates the fixture formula instead of measuring drift
description:
Sample: tests/test_store.py::test_the_drift_is_measured_rather_than_averaged_away claims detection_accuracy.feature 'Linear drift between the recording and the export' Then 'the drift is measured rather than averaged away' (and 'the punch-in is the intercept of the fit, not the middle of it').

labelled_corpus_pair already sets punch_in_seconds=1000.0, punch_out_seconds=3999.61, drift_ppm=-130.0. The test reloads those values and asserts punch_out == punch_in + 3000 * (1 + drift_ppm/1e6), which is how the fixture was built. Nothing measures a clock difference; the intercept-versus-middle Then is not asserted.

Storing a zeroed drift_ppm or an averaged punch_out does fail the test (the numbers are pinned), so this is not an UPDATE hole. It is the tautology hole: the assertion restates the fixture definition under the Gherkin's name.
acceptance_criteria: Either the test is renamed to a round-trip of stored drift_ppm and punch times, or it runs ground-truth extraction on a pair whose clocks differ. A fixture whose punch_out already equals punch_in + duration * (1 + drift_ppm/1e6) must not be the only thing asserting 'measured rather than averaged away'.

title: Overlap-refusal unit tests pass if the overlapping span is stored
description:
Sample: tests/test_extends_segment_span.py::test_extending_into_a_neighbouring_segment_is_refused (and test_covering_a_neighbour_is_refused, test_extending_the_end_into_a_neighbour_is_refused). Claims punch_point_adjustment.feature 'the change is rejected if it would overlap the neighbouring Segment'.

These tests only assert SpanWouldOverlapNeighbour is raised. Mutation that stayed green: ExtendsSegmentSpan saved the overlapping span and then raised. The three exception-only tests passed.

The Gherkin step and test_the_stored_span_is_unchanged_when_overlap_is_refused both reload the stored span and failed under that mutation. Covering a neighbour and extending the end have no persistence sibling, so those paths can store an overlap while the suite stays green except for the one start-extend sibling.

This is the same hole as sp-1vn.3: a refusal test that never checks nothing was stored.
acceptance_criteria: Each overlap-refusal test reloads the stored span and asserts it is unchanged, or shares a helper that does. Saving then raising SpanWouldOverlapNeighbour must fail those tests, not only test_the_stored_span_is_unchanged_when_overlap_is_refused.

title: Step 'punch-in may now be placed anywhere within the new span' only pins 1:27:00
description:
Sample: features/interface/punch_point_adjustment.feature · Extending a Segment beyond its detected span.

The Gherkin Then is 'the punch-in may now be placed anywhere within the new span'. tests/steps/interface/punch_point_adjustment_steps.py and tests/test_extends_segment_span.py::test_a_punch_in_may_sit_at_a_time_the_old_span_did_not_cover both place only 1:27:00 (inside the grown span, outside the old one) and persist it.

Mutation that stayed green: PlacesPunchIn refused every punch-in except exactly 1:27:00. The scenario and the companion unit test both passed.

The other two Thens in this scenario hold: span-grows fails if the start does not move earlier; overlap refusal reloads the stored span and fails if ExtendsSegmentSpan saves then raises.
acceptance_criteria: The Then asserts at least two times in the newly covered span (including the new start), or the Gherkin is narrowed to the one time actually placed. A mutation that accepts only 1:27:00 must fail.

title: The extracted pipeline hardcodes the ollama URL while config already has one
description: src/sermon/pipeline/classify.py carries OLLAMA = 'http://localhost:11434/...' from the spike, while src/sermon/config.py already provides SERMON_MODEL_ENDPOINT with HTTP-only validation, endpoint-naming errors, and an injected transport. acceptance_criteria: The pipeline reaches the model through the configured endpoint, and nothing hardcodes a host.

title: derive() computes speaker edges and discards them
description: segments.derive() assigns edges = speaker_edges(doc) and never reads the result. It is dead, and it calls diarization once per block to produce nothing. Moved verbatim during the extraction because that bead forbade refactoring. Two consequences worth acting on: the wasted diarization read per block, and the fact that speaker_edges was measured DEAD on the current corpus anyway — re-deriving all 181 stored block files with and without diarization gives identical fingerprints, because everything handed to snap() is already a transcript edge (refine_in/refine_out return utterance times), so a speaker edge can never win on distance. Decide whether speaker edges are meant to influence boundaries at all; if they are, the pipeline has a latent bug, and if they are not, the call and its data dependency should go.
acceptance_criteria: Either speaker edges influence a boundary and that is tested, or the call and its diarization dependency are removed.
close_reason: Removed unused speaker_edges assignment from derive(); speaker edges still influence snap via candidate_edges (already tested). Extraction follow-up, no Gherkin.

title: An import-hygiene guard is order-dependent on global state
description: tests/test_package_skeleton.py::test_no_package_loads_a_module_from_experiments scans ALL of sys.modules rather than what the five sermon packages import, so any test that legitimately loads an experiments module fails it depending on collection order — the suite read 598 rather than 597 until the baseline work unregistered its module after exec_module. The guard still asserts exactly the right thing; the defect is that it depends on global state it does not own, and the extraction beads (sp-79y.2, sp-79y.3) will be loading experiments modules constantly. Fix before them, or the next person debugs a phantom failure.
acceptance_criteria: The guard inspects what the sermon packages import, not the whole of sys.modules, and passes regardless of collection order.
close_reason: Hygiene guard walks the sermon package import graph instead of all of sys.modules; passes regardless of collection order.

title: Extending a Segment's span is not rejected when it overlaps its neighbour
description: interface/punch_point_adjustment.feature:201 'And the change is rejected if it would overlap the neighbouring Segment'. sp-1i8 gave Segment span_start_seconds and span_end_seconds, which makes the rule expressible, but nothing enforces it: the check compares two Segments of one Recording, so it cannot be a single-row constraint and belongs to the adjustment behaviour that owns the message the reviewer is shown. Sibling of sp-6kh, which owns the single-row invariants including punch points falling inside the span.
acceptance_criteria: Extending or moving a Segment's span is refused when it would overlap a neighbouring Segment of the same Recording, with the reason the scenario states.
close_reason: ExtendsSegmentSpan refuses a span that would overlap a neighbour on the same Recording, with the scenario's reason; touching and other recordings do not block.

title: Sidecar absence and the source of started_at are not recorded
description: recording_download.feature:43 'And the missing sidecar is noted on the Recording / And recorded_at falls back to the object's last-modified timestamp'. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic: the 10:50-10:57 start-time band is a confidence input (DOMAIN.md:50), so an upload-time fallback silently poisons scoring with no way to tell which Recordings are affected.
acceptance_criteria: A Recording records whether its start time came from the key or from a fallback, and scoring can tell.
close_reason: Recording.started_at_source, required and closed to key/last_modified, plus sidecar_present. Required with no default because a null reading as 'probably the key' is the same silent poisoning of the 10:50-10:57 confidence band that the bead exists to prevent. The sidecar's and webhook's recorded_at are not further values: each carries the recorded time the key already gives.

title: NEW ENTITY: the detection-accuracy corpus
description: detection_accuracy.feature needs one record per source/edit pair and none of the nine entities can hold any of it: :18 'And the derived boundaries are stored as the expected answer for that pair', :45 'Then that pair is excluded from the corpus / And the exclusion is reported rather than silently dropped', :58 clock drift 'measured rather than averaged away' (the -130 ppm fit), :72 'And its provenance is stored, not inferred later from the audio', :251 'Then each pair is graded against the difficulty of its own transition'. close_reason: CorpusPair in the application store: one record per source/edit pair, unique on recording+classification+provenance. Exclusions, drift fits (ppm and intercept-as-punch-in) and machine-cut provenance are stored fields, not inferred from audio or frozen experiments. title: Five DOMAIN.md statements are stale or falsified by scenarios

The fields are already nullable; the reasoning is wrong and will mislead the next reader.
acceptance_criteria: Every statement in DOMAIN.md is true of the spec as it stands, and settled questions are out of the does-not-decide section.
close_reason: DOMAIN.md now matches the spec: no hard delete in v1, one analysis, local FLAC reclaim, hand-drawn Segments have no seed Block, and the publication label is suggested from the summary. Settled questions left the does-not-decide section; only storage engine remains.

title: punch_in_difficulty names two different quantities
description: punch_in_detection.feature:64 has the system grade the cut it made, while detection_accuracy.feature:218 requires the scored difficulty come from the HUMAN cut and be unchangeable by the configuration being measured. Proposal.punch_in_difficulty currently carries one name for both. Whichever is renamed, the scoring one must be immune to the configuration under test -- that is the property the accuracy suite depends on.
acceptance_criteria: The system's grade of its own cut and the ground-truth difficulty of a transition are separately named.
close_reason: Proposal punch_in_grade/punch_out_grade is the machine's grade of its own cut; CorpusPair punch_in_difficulty/punch_out_difficulty is the scored human-cut quantity a configuration cannot change.

title: SpeakerProfile enrolment is Recording-grained but should be Segment-grained

Coincides today only because there is usually one teaching Segment per Recording.
acceptance_criteria: enrolled_from names the Segments that contributed, so un-enrolling removes exactly one voice.
close_reason: enrolled_from names Segments (int segment_id FK). Un-enrolling one of a lesson+sermon on the same Recording leaves the other. Profile is created, Segment is created, then enrolled_from is updated.

title: Segment cannot hold its warning flags
description: punch_in_detection.feature:124 'And the Segment is flagged check the opening', :143 recording-started-late; segment_proposal.feature:155 'And a boundary that cannot satisfy these is flagged rather than moved silently'; audio_rendering.feature:120 'And the Segment is flagged source was very quiet'. Excluded as derivable: no clean cut point (punch_in_difficulty/punch_out_difficulty), length outside range (the boundaries), started-late/stopped-early (a boundary at 0 or at duration). Not derivable: check-the-opening (a false start was detected), an unsatisfiable invariant, and source-was-very-quiet.

Review found the original three were short by two: 'no clean cut point found at punch-in' and its punch-out twin are quoted in the Gherkin and are NOT derivable from the Proposal's hard difficulty, which also grades noise near the cut and music under the first words.

title: Recording cannot hold its warning flags

Deliberately excluded as derivable: 'no substantive content' and 'no audio content' (dynamic_range_db, active_fraction) and 'suspiciously short/long' (duration). The clipping flag is filed separately and belongs in the same collection.
acceptance_criteria: A Recording carries an ordered set of named flags, several at once, and the detail view shows them.
close_reason: Recording.warnings[] holds seven named conditions from a closed set, ordered. Closed because later behaviour reads the strings — the render gates on one and the detail view explains another specifically — unlike Notification.kind and LogEntry.kind, which nothing branches on. Four conditions excluded as derivable from the emptiness metrics and duration.

title: Nothing injects a clock, and the log is all timestamps
description: The store takes occurred_at as data, so the processing-log work needed no clock and none was added -- correctly, rather than adding an unused dependency. But every LogEntry carries a timestamp, and whatever records transitions and attempts will need a clock that a test can substitute without patching globals or sleeping. CONVENTIONS.md's LS-003 rule is explicit: dependencies injected with defaults so a test can substitute the model host or the clock without patching globals. Decide the seam once, when the first writer exists, rather than letting each caller reach for datetime.now.
acceptance_criteria: A single injected clock seam exists and the log's writers use it; no test patches a global or sleeps.

comments.author: Travis Petticrew
comments.text: 2026-09-20: log writers on download/analyze/render/probe/waveform/reconcile/approve inject clock= with a default now(). Tests pass a frozen clock; they do not patch globals. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves a pre-existing database's old proposal table intact plus an orphaned block_speaker_profile, and the first Proposal write fails with 'OperationalError: table proposal has no column named proposal_id' -- verified by opening a baseline-written database with head code. title: An alternative punch-in candidate is specified but unmodelled

No DOMAIN.md field holds it. Outside the scope of all six domain-alignment beads; found while deciding the Proposal 1:1-vs-1:N fork.
acceptance_criteria: The alternative candidate is modelled and round-trips, or the scenario is changed.

title: Machine-proposed boundaries stay on the Segment, so a superseded Proposal loses its cuts
description: Proposal became 1:N with a supersession chain under sp-9dl, but the boundaries were left on the Segment rather than duplicated onto the Proposal, to avoid the two-sources-of-truth this model refuses elsewhere. The consequence, now written into DOMAIN.md's does-not-decide section: a superseded Proposal keeps its reasoning but not its cuts. reprocessing.feature wants boundary history, which needs an approver and a timestamp nothing currently holds -- so this is entangled with the processing log bead.
acceptance_criteria: Either the Proposal carries the boundaries it proposed, or the boundary history lives somewhere that satisfies reprocessing.feature.
close_reason: Boundary history lives on the log, so a superseded Proposal gets its cuts back via proposal_id and a reviewer's adjustment (which has no Proposal) sits in the same ordered history. Segment.proposed_punch_in was dropped rather than kept: it duplicated the machine's suggestion two rows above the model's own rule against a second source of truth, and nothing could have detected the drift.

title: Proposal is 1:1 but the spec requires proposal history

The same file also promises 'the retry is visible in the Recording's processing log', and there is no log entity. Either Proposal becomes 1:N with a supersession chain (Artifact already has superseded_by as precedent) or the scenarios are wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal history and the processing log are either modelled or the scenarios are changed to match.
close_reason: Proposal is 1:N with a supersession chain. Decided on the live requirement rather than the archival one: showing a new machine proposal beside a reviewer's edit needs two Proposals for one Segment simultaneously, which no 1:1 can hold. Boundaries deliberately stay on the Segment; the consequence and the missing processing log are both filed.

That scenario is tagged @measured -- identification was measured at 4 of 4 leave-one-out -- so the number exists and simply has no home.
acceptance_criteria: The speaker-to-block link carries a match confidence, and the store round-trips it.
close_reason: Block.speaker_profile_ids became Block.speaker_matches carrying a similarity per link. Named similarity rather than confidence because this model reserves confidence for a derived high/medium/low.

The store was built with ten because the sp-1vn.3 acceptance criterion names README's table as the authority. DOMAIN.md is most likely just stale -- but one of the two documents is wrong and a reader cannot tell which. sp-1vn.3's bead description inherited the same wrong count.
acceptance_criteria: The two documents agree, and the store's closed set matches.

title: validate_spec counts scenarios by regex, so its summary line can be forged

The harness now pins the summary string 'spec OK - 34 files, 460 scenarios, 142 rules', so a forgeable count weakens that guard. Executed during review: deleting a real scenario, adding one Examples row elsewhere, and adding a 'Scenario: not a real scenario' line inside a Gherkin docstring together kept the summary at 460 scenarios and 604 collected with all guard tests green, while the spec was genuinely one scenario lighter. A single fake docstring line alone moves the count to 461. title: sp-9ij extra pins landed in Green without a preceding Red
description: Green c274ab0 added tests that never went Red: pending-notification-not-sent-after-opt-out, recipient joins Reviewer on the actor seam, glance does not draw Reviewer as a FK, SpeakerProfile remains the one place a person is stored. Schema pins also landed in Green 2b939bd. The core store and send-time paths did have Red commits. These are extra pins of already-green behaviour, not missing coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Either the extra pins are accepted as Green-side characterisation tests, or they are split so each had a failing test first. No production change required unless a pin is wrong.

title: New-entity Red stubs make pytest ERROR rather than FAIL
description: sp-9ij's first Red shipped an empty Reviewer dataclass so Reviewer(actor=..., receives_notifications=True) TypeError'd. Pytest reports that as ERROR, not FAIL. ADR-LS-001 wants a failing assertion. The same empty-stub pattern was used for Discovery and SkippedObject ('so the tests fail on the fields they ask for instead of erroring on the import'). Decide whether new-entity Reds should carry the fields (and fail on missing persistence) or whether the established stub stays the convention.
acceptance_criteria: A stated convention for new-entity Red: either empty stubs are allowed, or a failing (not erroring) Red is shown for one entity and the others left as follow-up.

title: sp-d9a Red suite included a lock that already passed
description: tests/test_domain_md.py::test_agreement_gap_seconds_is_still_a_proposal_field passed against parent DOMAIN.md because agreement_gap_seconds already existed. It is a lock, not a Red failure. The other four tests in that commit did fail. Reviewer finding on sp-d9a, left as Minor.
acceptance_criteria: A Red commit's new tests fail on the parent tree, or a passing lock is not labelled Red.

title: AUDIT.md still claims two @needs-decision tags remain
description: sp-d9a removed the last @needs-decision claim from DOMAIN.md. AUDIT.md:345 still says two @needs-decision tags remain in the whole spec (second analysis agreement signal, and whether a hard delete exists). Both are settled: analysis_confidence.feature Rule 'v1 runs one analysis, and says so'; discarding_recordings.feature 'not in v1. There is no hard delete'. STATE.md already records both. Reviewer finding on sp-d9a, left as Minor.
acceptance_criteria: features/AUDIT.md does not claim @needs-decision tags remain after the spec settled them.
